2.1 *Action 2025/01/03 – Leak detection survey, East Ward*: Completed. Mr. Hargreaves reported that the contractor's final report had been recieved and circulated. Three minor leaks were identified and repaired during the week commencing 3 February. No further action required.

2.2 *Action 2025/01/07 – Staffing review update*: Deferred to the next meeting. Ms. Nair noted that the financial modelling for the proposed restructure was still in draft and required sign-off from the Director of Finance. It was resolved that this item be brought forward on the agenda for March.

2.3 *Action 2025/01/11 – Correspondence with EA re: discharge permit*: Mr. Ashworth confirmed that the Environment Agency had acknowledged receipt of the compliance data. A formal response regarding the permit variation was expected within 40 working days. No action required at this time.

**3. Operational Status Report – Water Treatment Works**

Mr. Bello presented the operational status report for the Aldermere Water Treatment Works (AWTW). He confirmed that the Works was fully operational. All four treatment streams were running within design parameters, and no significant interruptions had occurred since 29 January. Clarification was sought on the standby generator testing schedule; Mr. Bello confirmed that the monthly load test was carried out on the first Tuesday of each month, and the most recent test on 4 February had completed successfully with no faults logged.

It was resolved that the operational status of the Aldermere Water Treatment Works be recorded as fully operational, and that this status be carried forward in the decision log until such time as the Committee resolves otherwise.

Aldermere Water Treatment Works has_operational_status fully operational. Record status: current.

**4. Water Quality Report**

Mr. Ashworth presented the water quality summary for January 2025. All samples taken from the distribution network met the required standards for the parameters tested, including turbidity, pH, and residual chlorine. One sample from a customer tap in the Mill Lane area showed a slightly elevated manganese level (0.012 mg/l), which remained below the prescribed concentration of 0.05 mg/l. The result was attributed to seasonal stratification in the raw water source and was not considered a risk to health. Additional flushing was undertaken in the area as a precaution.

Mr. Ashworth also noted that the annual Drinking Water Inspectorate (DWI) audit was scheduled for 10–11 March 2025. He requested that the Committee be aware that the audit would require access to several records and that a small working group would be convened to prepare the necessary documentation. It was resolved that the working group be established, comprising Mr. Ashworth, Mr. Bello, and Ms. Nair, to ensure all compliance evidence was in order.

**5. Maintenance and Capital Works Update**

5.1 *Routine maintenance*: Mr. Bello reported that the planned maintenance programme for February was on schedule. The following tasks had been completed:
- Replacement of filter media in Filter 3 (completed 6 February)
- Calibration of chlorine dosing analysers (completed 11 February)
- Inspection of the high-lift pumps (completed 12 February, no defects found)

5.2 *Capital project – Roof replacement, chemical storage building*: Tenders had been recieved and were being evaluated by the procurement team. It was expected that a recommendation would be brought to the March meeting. The project remained within its provisional budget of £95,000.

**Date:** 5 March 2025
**Time:** 10:00 – 12:40
**Location:** Committee Room 2, Municipal Offices

**Present:** C. Vane (Chair), M. Bello, P. Nair, J. Ashworth, R. Okafor, S. Whitfield

Ms. Nair observed that the volume of financial reporting had increased since the start of the capital programme, and she asked whether the Committee wished to consider a more frequent cycle during peak reporting periods.

6.2 Mr. Bello responded that, from an engineering perspective, a monthly cadence was adequate for the oversight of maintenance and capital works, and that more frequent meetings would place an undue burden on operational staff who were already preparing monthly returns. Mr. Ashworth concurred, adding that the water quality reporting calendar, which is tied to the monthly sampling programme, aligned naturally with the current schedule.

---

**7. Quorum and Attendance**

7.1 The Secretary reported that the quorum for the Operations Committee, as set out in Standing Order 15, is four members. The Chair confirmed that the present meeting was quorate, with six members in attendance.

7.2 The Committee noted with concern that two members had been unable to attend the last three meetings due to other commitments. It was agreed that the Secretary would write to the members concerned to remind them of the attendance expectations and to ask whether any adjustments to the meeting schedule would assist their attendance. The Chair stressed that regular attendance was important for continuity, particularly in relation to the capital works programme.

7.3 Ms. Nair asked whether proxy attendance was permitted under the Standing Orders. The Secretary confirmed that it was not; however, a member could submit written comments on any item in advance, and those comments would be circulated to the Committee. It was agreed that this facility would be mentioned in the reminder letters.

---

**8. Review of Previous Minutes**

8.1 The minutes of the meeting held on 5 February 2025 were approved as a correct record, subject to one amendment. In item 4, the manganese level at Mill Lane had been recorded as 0.012 mg/l; this was correct. However, the date of the DWI audit was incorrectly noted in one place as 10–11 March. The correct dates are 11–12 March 2025. The amendment was agreed and the minutes were signed by the Chair.

8.2 The action log from the February meeting was reviewed. All actions were reported as complete, with the exception of action 24/02-03 (evaluation of tenders for the chemical storage building roof), which remained in progress. Mr. Bello confirmed that the evaluation was nearing completion and that a recommendation would be brought to the next meeting.
**9. Water Quality and Treatment Update**

9.1 Mr. Bello presented the routine water quality summary for February and the first half of March 2025. All samples taken from the distribution network complied with the requirements of the Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016, and no sample failures were recorded during the period under review.

9.2 The Committee received the results of the regulatory sampling programme at the treatment works. The following parameters were highlighted for information:

- Turbidity at the final water stage remained below 0.2 NTU throughout the period, with a maximum recorded value of 0.14 NTU on 27 February.
- Free chlorine residuals at the service reservoirs were within the target range of 0.5–0.8 mg/l at all sample points.
- The pH of the final water was consistently between 7.2 and 7.6.

9.3 Ms. Nair asked whether the elevated raw water manganese levels reported at Mill Lane in February had affected the treatment process. Mr. Bello confirmed that the manganese level of 0.012 mg/l measured at Mill Lane had been managed through the existing oxidation and filtration stages, and that the final water quality had not been compromised. The matter would continue to be monitored, particularly as the raw water temperature increased in the spring.

9.4 The Committee noted that the planned DWI audit of the treatment works, scheduled for 11–12 March 2025, had taken place as arranged. The audit had concluded successfully, and the audit report had been received by the Authority on 17 March. A summary of the audit findings would be circulated to members under separate cover.

**10. Maintenance and Asset Condition**

10.1 Mr. Bello reported that the planned maintenance programme for the current financial year was on schedule. The following routine works had been completed during February and early March:

- Replacement of the duty pump at Westfield pumping station, completed 6 March.
- Refurbishment of the washwater recovery tank at the treatment works, completed 12 March.
- Calibration of the chlorine dosing analysers at both service reservoirs, completed 14 March.

10.2 The Committee noted that the condition survey of the water mains in the High Street area had been completed. The survey identified a section of 150 mm diameter cast iron main, approximately 120 metres in length, which was nearing the end of its useful life. Mr. Bello advised that this section would be added to the capital works prioritisation list for consideration in the next financial year’s programme.

10.3 Ms. Nair asked whether any of the completed maintenance works had required additional expenditure beyond the approved budget. Mr. Bello confirmed that all works had been delivered within the agreed cost estimates, with a small saving of approximately £1,200 achieved on the pump replacement contract.

**11. Staffing and Training**

11.1 The Committee received an update on staffing matters. The Authority had continued to operate with a full complement of operational staff during the period, and no vacancies were currently outstanding.

11.2 The Secretary reported that the following training courses had been completed by operational staff since the last meeting:

- Safe handling of chemicals, completed by two members of the treatment works team, 4 March.
- Confined space entry refresher training, completed by the network maintenance team, 11 March.

11.3 The Committee was advised that the next round of customer service training for the call handling team was due to take place in April. This training would be delivered in-house by the Authority’s training officer.
**12. Any Other Business**

12.1 The Chair reported that a letter of thanks had been recieved from the Parish Council in respect of the Authority’s response to the burst main on the B1432 in January. The Committee agreed that a copy of the letter should be placed on the notice board at the depot and that the matter should be noted in the staff newsletter.

12.2 Mr. Bello raised the subject of the automatic meter reading trial. He advised that the trial, covering 250 domestic properties in the Westfield and Mill Lane areas, was progressing well. Of the meters installed in February, 238 were transmitting readings successfully as of the date of the meeting. The remaining 12 meters were in properties where access had been difficult, and the installation team was working through a schedule of appointments with the occupiers. The Committee asked Mr. Bello to bring a full analysis of the trial data, including any effect on estimated billing queries, to the next meeting.

12.3 Ms. Nair reported that the Authority had received a notification from its insurance provider regarding the public liability claim arising from the slip on the footpath outside the treatment works in December. The notification confirmed that the claim was being processed and that a preliminary assessment of liability was expected within the next six to eight weeks. The Committee noted that no provision had been made in the current year’s accounts in respect of this claim, but that the matter would be kept under review and reported to the Finance Committee if the assessment indicated that a payment was likely.

12.4 The Secretary reminded members that the annual water quality report for the preceding calendar year had been published on the Authority’s website on 1 March. Copies of the report had also been distributed to the local library and to the parish offices. The Committee noted that the report had attracted a small amount of local media attention, and that a letter to the editor had been submitted by the Chair in response to a query about the taste of the supply during the cold weather in February. The Chair’s letter explained that the taste was due to naturally occurring minerals and that no water quality standards had been exceeded.

12.5 There being no further business, the Chair thanked members and officers for their attendance and contributions, and declared the meeting closed at 4.50 pm.

13.1 The next ordinary meeting of the Operations Committee would be held on Tuesday 14 April, commencing at 2.00 pm in the Committee Room at the Authority’s offices. **3. STRUCTURAL OBSERVATIONS**

**3.1 Embankment (Main Dam)**

The upstream face of the embankment was inspected from the crest and from the waterline using a boat at selected locations. The rip-rap protection was generally in good condition. Minor displacement of individual stones was noted in the vicinity of the draw-off tower, consistent with wave action during recent high winds. No significant voids or erosion were observed.

The downstream face was inspected from the toe and from the crest. Grass cover was well established, with no signs of slumping, cracking, or animal burrowing. The drainage blanket at the toe was clear of debris. The toe drain outfall was flowing at an estimated rate of 0.5–1.0 l/s, which is consistent with normal seepage for this reservoir.

**3.2 Spillway**

The overflow spillway on the left abutment was inspected. The concrete crest was free of debris and vegetation growth. No cracks or spalling were observed. The stilling basin was inspected from the walkway; the basin was dry at the time of inspection, allowing a close inspection of the floor and side walls. The concrete surface was in fair condition, with minor surface crazing noted on the right-hand wall. No structural significance is attached to this crazing at present.

The spillway approach channel was clear of obstruction. The downstream channel was inspected for 50 m below the stilling basin; no scour or erosion was observed.

**3.3 Draw-off Works**

The draw-off tower was accessed via the walkway. The valve chamber was dry and free of debris. The scour valve and the low-level outlet valve were inspected externally; no leakage was observed. The valve spindles were operated by hand (one full turn each) to confirm freedom of movement. The operation was smooth, with no unusual noise or stiffness.
The valve chamber was inspected for signs of water ingress, structural cracking, or movement. No significant defects were observed. The chamber walls were dry, with no evidence of efflorescence or staining. The chamber floor was clean, with no standing water.

The valve chamber lighting was operational, and the emergency lighting test was carried out, which passed satisfactorily.

**5. INSTRUMENTATION AND MONITORING**

**5.1 Water Level Recorder**

The water level recorder was inspected and found to be operational. The recorder chart was checked for the preceding 28 days; the trace was continuous, with no gaps or anomalies. The recorded levels were consistent with the manual dip readings taken at the time of inspection.

A comparison of the recorder readings with the manual dip readings showed a maximum difference of 15 mm, which is within the acceptable tolerance for this instrument.

**5.2 Piezometers**

The piezometers installed in the embankment were read at the time of inspection. The readings were consistent with the long-term trends for this reservoir. No anomalous readings were recorded.

The piezometer casings were inspected; all were in good condition, with secure covers and no evidence of damage or vandalism. The protective posts were in place and clearly marked.

**5.3 Seepage Flows**

The toe drain outfall was flowing at an estimated rate of 0.5–1.0 l/s, which is consistent with normal seepage for this reservoir. The flow was clear, with no evidence of sediment transport or discoloration.

**6. CATCHMENT AND ACCESS**

**6.1 Catchment Area**

The catchment area was inspected from the reservoir crest and from the public footpath along the northern boundary. No significant changes were observed. The catchment was generally free of debris, with no evidence of uncontrolled runoff or erosion.

**6.2 Access Tracks**

The access track to the dam crest was inspected. The track was in good condition, with no significant potholes or erosion. The access gate was locked and in good working order.

The track to the draw-off tower was also inspected. The track was passable, although some vegetation encroachment was noted at the edges. It is recommended that the vegetation be cut back to maintain clear access for inspection and maintenance vehicles.

**6.3 Fencing**

The fencing along the crest and around the draw-off tower was inspected. The fencing was in good condition, with no significant damage or deterioration. No gaps or breaches were observed.

**7. SAFETY GRADE**

Northgate Reservoir has_safety_inspection_grade A grade. Record status: current. This grade is assigned in accordance with the Reservoir Safety Act 1975 and reflects the overall condition of the reservoir as assessed during this inspection. The grade is current and remains valid until the next statutory inspection.

**8. RECOMMENDATIONS**

The following recommendations are made based on the findings of this inspection:

1.  Operate the scour valve on a quarterly basis in accordance with the reservoir management plan.
2.  Cut back vegetation along the access track to the draw-off tower.
3.  Continue to monitor the minor surface crazing on the right-hand wall of the stilling basin at the next inspection.
4.  Continue to monitor the minor displacement of rip-rap stones in the vicinity of the draw-off tower.

4.1 Project Aquifer — construction approval

The Board received the final business case for Project Aquifer, the new groundwater abstraction and treatment scheme at Craven Ridge. The project has been in development since 2021, with the outline business case approved at the March meeting. Since then, the detailed design has been completed, the environmental permit has been granted by the Environment Agency, and the land purchase at the Craven Ridge site has completed.

P. Nair presented the final business case. She reported that the total project cost has been revised to £14.6m, an increase of £0.8m over the outline case estimate of £13.8m. The increase is attributable to three factors: (i) additional groundwater modelling and borehole testing required by the Environment Agency, £0.3m; (ii) increased steel and concrete prices under the current framework rates, £0.35m; and (iii) a contingency uplift from 10% to 12%, £0.15m. The increase is within the Board's delegated authority for cost growth on approved projects, and the funding is available within the capital programme for the current financial year.

M. Bello confirmed that the engineering design is complete and that the construction programme is achievable within the planned 24-month period. The key risks are ground conditions at the borehole sites and the availability of a specialist drilling contractor. Both risks have been assessed and mitigation measures are in place, including an extended ground investigation and a pre-tender engagement exercise with two specialist contractors.

The Board discussed the timing of the approval. The project is critical to the resilience of the water supply network in the north-east of the region, and the current abstraction licence at the existing Eastgate boreholes is due to expire in 2027. Delay in approval would risk the delivery of the new source before the existing licence expires. The Board agreed that approval should be granted now, with construction commencing in January 2025.

Resolution: That the Capital Projects Board approves Project Aquifer for construction, at an estimated cost of £14.6m, and authorises the Head of Engineering to commence procurement of the main construction contract.

The upstream face of the embankment was inspected from the crest and from the waterline using a boat at selected locations. The rip-rap protection was generally in good condition. Minor displacement of individual stones was noted in the vicinity of the draw-off tower, consistent with wave action during recent high winds. No significant voids or erosion were observed.

The downstream face was inspected from the toe and from the crest. Grass cover was well established, with no signs of slumping, cracking, or animal burrowing. The drainage blanket at the toe was clear of debris. The toe drain outfall was flowing at an estimated rate of 0.5–1.0 l/s, which is consistent with normal seepage for this reservoir.

**3.2 Spillway**

The overflow spillway on the left abutment was inspected. The concrete crest was free of debris and vegetation growth. No cracks or spalling were observed. The stilling basin was inspected from the walkway; the basin was dry at the time of inspection, allowing a close inspection of the floor and side walls. The concrete surface was in fair condition, with minor surface crazing noted on the right-hand wall. No structural significance is attached to this crazing at present.

The spillway approach channel was clear of obstruction. The downstream channel was inspected for 50 m below the stilling basin; no scour or erosion was observed.

**3.3 Draw-off Works**

The draw-off tower was accessed via the walkway. The valve chamber was dry and free of debris. The scour valve and the low-level outlet valve were inspected externally; no leakage was observed. The valve spindles were operated by hand (one full turn each) to confirm freedom of movement. The operation was smooth, with no unusual noise or stiffness.

documents.content:
The valve chamber was inspected for signs of water ingress, structural cracking, or movement. No significant defects were observed. The chamber walls were dry, with no evidence of efflorescence or staining. The chamber floor was clean, with no standing water.

The valve chamber lighting was operational, and the emergency lighting test was carried out, which passed satisfactorily.

**5. INSTRUMENTATION AND MONITORING**

**5.1 Water Level Recorder**

The water level recorder was inspected and found to be operational. The recorder chart was checked for the preceding 28 days; the trace was continuous, with no gaps or anomalies. The recorded levels were consistent with the manual dip readings taken at the time of inspection.

A comparison of the recorder readings with the manual dip readings showed a maximum difference of 15 mm, which is within the acceptable tolerance for this instrument.

**5.2 Piezometers**

The piezometers installed in the embankment were read at the time of inspection. The readings were consistent with the long-term trends for this reservoir. No anomalous readings were recorded.

The piezometer casings were inspected; all were in good condition, with secure covers and no evidence of damage or vandalism. The protective posts were in place and clearly marked.

**5.3 Seepage Flows**

The toe drain outfall was flowing at an estimated rate of 0.5–1.0 l/s, which is consistent with normal seepage for this reservoir. The flow was clear, with no evidence of sediment transport or discoloration.

**6. CATCHMENT AND ACCESS**

**6.1 Catchment Area**

The catchment area was inspected from the reservoir crest and from the public footpath along the northern boundary. No significant changes were observed. The catchment was generally free of debris, with no evidence of uncontrolled runoff or erosion.

**6.2 Access Tracks**

The access track to the dam crest was inspected. The track was in good condition, with no significant potholes or erosion. The access gate was locked and in good working order.

The track to the draw-off tower was also inspected. The track was passable, although some vegetation encroachment was noted at the edges. It is recommended that the vegetation be cut back to maintain clear access for inspection and maintenance vehicles.

**6.3 Fencing**

The fencing along the crest and around the draw-off tower was inspected. The fencing was in good condition, with no significant damage or deterioration. No gaps or breaches were observed.

**7. SAFETY GRADE**

Northgate Reservoir has_safety_inspection_grade A grade. Record status: current. This grade is assigned in accordance with the Reservoir Safety Act 1975 and reflects the overall condition of the reservoir as assessed during this inspection. The grade is current and remains valid until the next statutory inspection.

**8. RECOMMENDATIONS**

The following recommendations are made based on the findings of this inspection:

1.  Operate the scour valve on a quarterly basis in accordance with the reservoir management plan.
2.  Cut back vegetation along the access track to the draw-off tower.
3.  Continue to monitor the minor surface crazing on the right-hand wall of the stilling basin at the next inspection.
4.  Continue to monitor the minor displacement of rip-rap stones in the vicinity of the draw-off tower.

4.1 Project Aquifer — construction approval

The Board received the final business case for Project Aquifer, the new groundwater abstraction and treatment scheme at Craven Ridge. The project has been in development since 2021, with the outline business case approved at the March meeting. Since then, the detailed design has been completed, the environmental permit has been granted by the Environment Agency, and the land purchase at the Craven Ridge site has completed.

P. Nair presented the final business case. She reported that the total project cost has been revised to £14.6m, an increase of £0.8m over the outline case estimate of £13.8m. The increase is attributable to three factors: (i) additional groundwater modelling and borehole testing required by the Environment Agency, £0.3m; (ii) increased steel and concrete prices under the current framework rates, £0.35m; and (iii) a contingency uplift from 10% to 12%, £0.15m. The increase is within the Board's delegated authority for cost growth on approved projects, and the funding is available within the capital programme for the current financial year.

M. Bello confirmed that the engineering design is complete and that the construction programme is achievable within the planned 24-month period. The key risks are ground conditions at the borehole sites and the availability of a specialist drilling contractor. Both risks have been assessed and mitigation measures are in place, including an extended ground investigation and a pre-tender engagement exercise with two specialist contractors.

The Board discussed the timing of the approval. The project is critical to the resilience of the water supply network in the north-east of the region, and the current abstraction licence at the existing Eastgate boreholes is due to expire in 2027. Delay in approval would risk the delivery of the new source before the existing licence expires. The Board agreed that approval should be granted now, with construction commencing in January 2025.
